_doc: r03 render configuration (from r02). gain_dB: static stem gain; pan: -1 left .. +1 right; width: 0 mono .. 1 sample's own stereo; src: Detmold Konzerthaus loudspeaker-orchestra source; send_dB: reverb send relative to the dry stem; family: rule set for articulations; engine: fluidsynth (FluidR3_GM) or sfz (sfzplay.py with the files in sfz.channels, one per MIDI channel); accent_extra_vel: velocity added to accented notes.

master._doc_eq: r04: zero-phase mix-bus EQ (lib/busq.py). r05 (critic 4, plan 5): retuned against the mean third-octave LTAS of all four Brahms references (1 and 4, I and II; meas/scripts/eqtune4.py): the 6.3 kHz bell (Q 1.0) moved to 7 kHz Q 1.8 and a -0.7 dB bell at 3 kHz (2.5-3.2 kHz was +2.5 dB), 720 Hz -2.0, low shelf +2 dB below 90 Hz (share < 100 Hz)
master._doc_eq_r06: r06: 720 Hz bell -2.0 -> -2.6 (794 Hz third octave +2.7 dB over the Brahms mean in m1), low shelf 90 Hz +2.0 -> +3.0 (62-79 Hz -3.1/-4.6 dB in m1; m2 -0.6/-0.9)

dynamics._doc: extra expression (CC11, dB) added to the velocity's own level, by velocity-equivalent of the printed dynamic; ppp 32, pp 42, p 53, mp 64, mf 74, f 84, ff 91, fff 110 after fff_velocity_cut (v120 volume table x 127). headroom_dB is taken off every CC11 curve and added back as stem gain. per_track_families: one CC11 curve per voice track.
dynamics._doc_r05: r05 (critic 4, plan 2): f -1.8 -> -2.3, ff -4.3 -> -4.8, fff -5.0 -> -5.5 (mf->f and f->ff bar steps 4.6-6.3 dB in both movements). A soft-end lift (+2 dB at <= p) was tested: m2 LRA 22.2 -> 20.9 but m1 LRA 18.7 -> 17.5 and m1 inversions outside hairpins 221 -> 274, so not kept (NOTES.md)
dynamics._doc_r06: r06 (critic 5, plan 8): printed_trim_all_dB is added to every stem's printed_trim_dB (articulate.py), one trim per PRINTED dynamic for the whole orchestra: ff/fff -1 dB (m2 LRA 21-22 LU against 15-17 in the slow references; a further f -1 was tested: m2 LRA 20.9 -> 20.4 but m1 LRA 17.9 and m1 bars <= mf louder than the median f bar 12 -> 15, so not kept)

articulation._doc_timp_roll_curve: r05 (critic 4, plan 1): each recorded roll's CC11 curve is built from the dynamics and hairpins printed inside it (notes.csv inner; articulate.roll_curve): step_dB per printed step, hairpins ramp to the next printed dynamic, settle (settle_dB, tau, then sink_dB_per_bar after sink_after_s, at most settle_max_dB) only between them, restarting at each new dynamic. timp_roll_long_* are unused in r05.
articulation._doc_accent_r06: r06 (Dan 2026-10-10, critic 5 plan 2): accent_mode weight: an accented note takes the plain notes' velocity (LilyPond already adds +20, marcato +40) raised by accent_level_dB on the velocity law 40*log10(v/127) for the whole note (stems.<staff>.accent_level_dB overrides; accent_vel_steps, an additive velocity, is used only where no accent_level_dB is set; marcato x marcato_scale), stays on the sustain channel (string_accent_channel false: no VPO accent samples), and gets a CC11 bump of accent_bump_dB reached in accent_bump_rise_s, back over accent_bump_fall_s; no accent dip (sf / fp keep theirs). accent_extra_vel is unused in this mode.
articulation._doc_roll_r06: r06 (critic 5, plan 4): after a hairpin reaches its printed target the roll settles at most timp_roll_post_hairpin_settle_dB; printed dynamics <= timp_roll_soft_max_dyn settle at most timp_roll_soft_settle_max_dB; the bar for the sink is the MIDI time signature's bar; balance.roll_carry_cut carries the largest roll cut into later segments unless a crescendo starts there; roll channel attack 5 ms (no sample-step front).
articulation._doc_hairpin_cap_r06: r06: a note under a printed hairpin plays at most the staff's plain median velocity of max(printed dynamic + hairpin_cap_steps, the staff's next printed dynamic) (LilyPond's MIDI let a pp swell with no target reach the ff velocity; articulate.py)
articulation._doc_roll_r07: r07 (critic 6, plan 1): timp_roll_chains: consecutive timpani tremolo notes with no gap are one roll (lib/marks.roll_chains) for the roll curve, start stroke, trims and the balance roll rule; a change of drum inside a chain keeps the earlier drum on channel 2 (roll samples without the closing stroke) overlapping the new one by timp_roll_chain_overlap_s.
articulation._doc_sf_r07: r07 (critic 6, plan 7): sf_mode weight: an sf note starts from the plain-note velocity (as accents) raised by sf_level_dB (40*log10 law) plus a CC11 bump of sf_bump_dB with the accent rise/fall (40 ms / 300 ms), instead of +sf_velocity_boost and a dip; fp keeps its recipe. Test B had level 4 / bump 2: the +4 dB lasted the whole note, so v203 bars 41-42 (tutti sf > decresc whole notes) rose 4 dB and became the movement's loudest moment (S max +6.7 -> +8.2 LU); level 1 + bump 3 keeps the sf an attack.

melodies._doc: r03: marked melodies are derived from the score's text marks (lib/marks.py): every text script matching pattern; phrase = from the bar of the staff's first note at/after the mark while the staff has notes in consecutive bars, at most max_bars. No bar numbers.

percussion._doc: printed DrumStaff events read by perc.py from the LilyPond source of the score being rendered (render.py --score); keys of sfz/perc-r02.sfz; l.v. notes held lv_s seconds; a crescendo roll uses the crescendo sample whose peak time is nearest the printed roll length
percussion._doc_r07: r07: bd (bass drum, key 36, VSCO 2 CE samples in sfz/perc-r07.sfz); perc.py reads drum chords <cymc bd>, drops \tweak, and plays a tied note as one stroke held for its written length (damped there, no l.v.)

balance_targets_dB._doc: target stem level relative to Violins I at the same printed dynamic (stems.py level while sounding); used by the calibration in NOTES.md section 3

balance._doc: r03 mix-stage balance (lib/balance.py), measured on the placed stems: melodies at least margin_dB over the loudest other stem (lift at most lift_max_dB, the rest as cuts on the competing stems, at most duck_max_dB), melody at least sum_margin_dB against the power sum of the others; timpani in rolls longer than a bar at least roll_margin_dB under the loudest other stem. r04: duck_same_dB caps the cut on a stem printed at the melody's dynamic (stems printed louder are never cut, softer at most duck_max_dB); tutti_frac: a bar is a tutti when at least this share of sounding stems is printed f or louder (no cuts; a melody phrase ends there when the melody is printed f or louder); preserve_dB: each bar's summed loudness stays within this of the no-balance bar; smooth_s 1.25 (fader slope a few dB/s); inv_margin_dB: a melody is lifted at most to this many dB over a sounding stem printed louder than it
balance._doc_r07: r07 (critic 6, plan 1): rolls are chains of untied roll notes (marks.roll_chains); roll_margin_cresc_dB 0.5 -> 1.5 (target: never within 1 dB of the loudest stem); roll_margin_step_dB: per printed step the timpani is printed softer than the loudest printed sounding stem, the roll sits this much further under it; roll_lead_if_printed_louder: no cut in a bar where the timpani is printed louder than every sounding stem.
balance._doc_spot_r07: r07 (critic 6, plan 5): spot_lift: where a marked melody is printed <= mf and at most spot_max_stems stems sound, all sounding stems rise together toward (median loudness of bars of the same printed dynamic + spot_target_dB), at most spot_lift_max_dB (lib/balance.py)
balance._doc_spot_r08: r08 (critic 7, plan 4): the spot lift also acts where a marked melody printed <= spot_soft_max_dyn sounds with up to spot_soft_max_stems stems and every other stem is printed at or below it; bars printed <= mp may rise up to spot_soft_lift_max_dB (lib/balance.py)

_doc_printed_trim: r03: stems.<staff>.printed_trim_dB: dB added to the CC11 curve while the PRINTED dynamic (notes.csv) is the given one. dyn_corr_dB (r02) is keyed on the velocity-equivalent of the MIDI velocity, which LilyPond scales per instrument (oboes ff = velocity 64), so its ff entries never reach most wind staves. Values: at ff these stems measured 3-8 dB above their balance target against Violins I in both movements (r03 meas, stemcmp).

timing._doc: r04 section timing (articulate.py): family_ms = [offset on soft entries (printed <= mp), offset otherwise] in ms, plus a random offset within +-random_ms held for each phrase_s segment, per staff. r04: tested and disabled (onset peak correlation fell 0.56 -> 0.55 in m1 and 0.29 -> 0.26 in m2, lag 60 -> 70 ms in m2; NOTES.md)
